# Component guide

One entry per component, copied from the design system. Props and types are in `packages/ui-web/src/index.d.ts`. For a live view of every component, open the design system gallery.

## Button

Group: Actions

Use Button for every action. Default is `secondary` (outlined); use `primary` (`light-blue` fill) at most once per screen, for the action the screen exists for.

- Provide: `children` (a verb first, plain words: "Send credits"), `onClick` or `type="submit"`.
- Member screens use `size="lg"` (52px tall) and an `icon` beside the label; never an icon alone.
- `size="sm"` only in manager tables and toolbars; `ghost` for low-weight actions; `danger` for suspending or closing.
- While an action runs, disable the button and change its label ("Sending…").

## TextField

Group: Forms

Use TextField for single-line input, always with a visible `label`.

- Provide: `label`, `value`/`onChange` (or `defaultValue`), and native input props.
- Member screens set `large`. Put the unit in `suffix` ("credits") so people type only the number.
- `hint` says what to type or what is available; `error` replaces it with an icon and a plain sentence of what to do.

## Select

Group: Forms

Use Select to pick one value from a short fixed list (up to about 10 options).

- Provide: `label`, `options` (strings or `{value, label}`), `value`/`onChange` or `defaultValue`.
- `placeholder` adds a disabled first option; pair it with `defaultValue=""`.
- Same `hint`/`error` behaviour as TextField.

## Card

Group: Layout

Use Card to group one topic on a dashboard or detail page; its title carries the manual's short green rule.

- Provide: `title`, `children`; optionally `subtitle`, `actions` (small buttons, top right) and `footer` (metadata on `surface-muted`).
- Set `flush` when the body is a DataTable, AccountList or TransactionList so rows run edge to edge.
- Place cards on `surface-muted`; cards themselves are `surface` with a `line` border and square corners, no shadow.

## Badge

Group: Status

Use Badge for a one- or two-word status beside a name or amount, mostly in manager screens.

- Provide: `children` (the word; colour never carries meaning alone) and `tone`: `success` (active, certified), `info` (measured, information), `warning` (estimated), `danger` (suspended), `neutral` (closed, manual).
- Text stays `ink` on the tinted grounds; only `danger` uses `danger` text.
- On member screens prefer a plain sentence or `InlineAlert` over a badge.

## InlineAlert

Group: Status

Use InlineAlert to tell people something important on the page: an outcome, a warning, or why something did not work.

- Provide: `tone` (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`), a short `title` and one plain sentence as `children`.
- Every tone has an icon and a border, so colour is never the only signal.
- Errors say what happened and what to do; after a failed send, say that no credits moved (the ledger rolls back any failed operation).

## Icon

Group: Status

Use Icon beside words to help people recognise an action or kind of activity at a glance.

- Provide: `name`. Icons are decorative by default; give `label` only when an icon stands alone, which member screens should avoid.
- The set is small and original: sun, wind, plug, battery, clock, coins, panel, wrench, heart, star, exchange, arrows, person, check, info, alert, search, chevron, back.
- Icons inherit the text colour.

## StatTile

Group: Dashboard

Use StatTile for one headline number on a manager dashboard, in a row of two to four.

- Provide: `label`, `value`, `unit`. Negative values show a minus sign.
- `accent` colours the top bar: `green` for energy figures, `light-blue` for platform and wallet figures, `orange` for community activity, following the manual's colour associations.
- `delta` adds a change line with an arrow and a word label.

## DataTable

Group: Dashboard

Use DataTable for rows of records with aligned columns.

- Provide: `columns` (`key`, `header`, optional `align: "right"` for numbers, optional `render`) and `rows`; `rowKey` names the id field (default `id`).
- `onRowClick` makes rows keyboard-focusable and clickable; `selectedKey` highlights a row in `light-blue-tint`.
- Right-align all quantities and include the unit in the cell.
- Give `emptyText` that says what will appear ("No member accounts yet.").

## Identifier

Group: Ledger

Use Identifier to show a wallet ID, transaction ID or hash in manager and support screens. Never show identifiers on member screens outside "Technical details".

- Provide: `value`; optional `label` names it for the Copy button ("transaction ID").
- Shortened by default with the full value on hover; `full` shows all of it.

## PurposeTag

Group: Ledger

Use PurposeTag to say what kind of activity a movement was. Members see an icon and plain words; managers can see the raw code.

- Provide: `code` (a purpose_code) or `txType`, and `direction` (`in` or `out`) so the wording fits ("Solar energy you shared", "Community energy you used").
- `technical` shows the raw code (`GEN_SOLAR`) for manager tables.
- The plain wording is a proposal and should be checked with members.

## ConfidenceBadge

Group: Ledger

Use ConfidenceBadge in manager and support screens to show how trustworthy the data behind a transaction is.

- Provide: `level`: `CERTIFIED`, `MEASURED`, `ESTIMATED` or `MANUAL`. The tooltip explains each in one line.
- Members see only "Estimated reading" where it applies, not this badge.

## WalletBalance

Group: Member

Use WalletBalance as the first thing a member sees: how many credits they have.

- Provide: `balance` (from the backend). Optional `available` if the backend reports a different spendable amount, `updated` (already formatted) and `actions` (large buttons: "Send credits", "Exchange").
- The number is large (48px) with the word "credits"; nothing else competes with it.
- A balance below zero is shown with a minus sign in the normal text colour, never red. Pass `negativeNote` with a plain explanation from the backend.

## BalanceStatement

Group: Member

Use BalanceStatement to show a member what changed in a period: the balance at the start, each kind of activity, and the balance at the end.

- Provide: `period`, `opening`, `closing` and `lines` (`direction`, `purposeCode` or `txType`, `amount`, optional `count`). All values come from the backend.
- Group many movements of one kind into one line with `count` rather than listing each.

## EnergySummary

Group: Member

Use EnergySummary to connect a member's electricity with their credits for a period.

- Provide: `used` (`communityKwh`, `supplierKwh`, optional `credits` and `supplierNote`) and optional `shared` (`kWh`, `credits`).
- It shows kWh and credit amounts only, never conversion factors or formulas; the backend computes the credits.
- Set `estimated` when any reading in the period was estimated.

## TransactionList

Group: Member

Use TransactionList for a member's recent activity, newest first.

- Provide: `transactions` (each with `direction`, `amount` and `purposeCode` or `txType`; `counterpartyName` for member-to-member transfers; `time` already formatted).
- Each row is an icon, one plain sentence, the date and a signed amount. Set `onSelect` to make whole rows open TransactionDetail (rows are at least 64px tall).
- Ledger records are final once written, so there is no "pending" or "failed" state here.

## TransactionDetail

Group: Member

Use TransactionDetail when a member or manager opens one movement.

- Provide: `transaction`. The top shows the amount and what it was in plain words, then when, who, energy and note.
- The full ledger record (IDs, wallets, purpose code, valuation rule, metering point, data quality, hashes) sits in a closed "Technical details" section for managers and support. Set `showTechnical={false}` to hide it entirely.

## RecipientPicker

Group: Member

Use RecipientPicker to choose who receives credits: a searchable list of people, never a typed address.

- Provide: `recipients` (`id` of the receiving wallet, `name`, optional `detail` such as a street) from the backend, `value`, `onChange`.
- Rows are 60px tall with initials, name and detail. Mark people who cannot receive with `disabled`.
- Which names and details members may see of each other is a privacy decision for the backend.

## TransferForm

Group: Member

Use TransferForm to send credits to another member in three steps: choose a person, enter an amount, check and send.

- Provide: `recipients`, `available` (from the backend), `onSubmit({ to, amount, note })`.
- Report progress with `status`: `working` while the backend acts, `done` with `newBalance`, or `error` with the backend's `errorCode` (`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` has its own message; others show a generic one saying no credits moved).
- The form checks only that the amount is above zero and not above `available`. All other rules (limits, minimum balances, eligibility) are the backend's.

## SettlementRequestForm

Group: Member

Use SettlementRequestForm when a member asks to exchange credits for money. It sends a request; it does not move credits.

- Provide: `available`, `onSubmit({ amount })`; optional `estimate(credits)` returning a formatted money amount when the backend can give one.
- The confirmation says the community manager must approve and that payment happens outside the app.
- Report progress with `status` as for TransferForm.

## AccountCard

Group: Manager

Use AccountCard in manager screens for one member and their wallets.

- Provide: `member` with `name`, `role`, `status` and `wallets` (`id`, `type`, `balance`, `status`, optional `label`).
- Balances are in EC with a minus sign when below zero; community and dependent wallets are normally below zero.
- `actions`: small buttons such as History and Suspend.

## AccountList

Group: Manager

Use AccountList in manager screens to list wallets with owner, type, ID, balance and status.

- Provide: `wallets` (`id`, `name`, `type`: `MEMBER`, `COMMUNITY` or `DEPENDENT`, `balance`, `status`: `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED` or `CLOSED`).
- `onSelect` + `selectedId` turn it into a master list for AccountCard.

## TopBar

Group: Shell

Use TopBar at the top of every INNO-TREC web tool.

- Provide: `logoSrc` (use `assets/Logos/logo-landscape-colour.png` on this white bar), `title` (the tool's name), optional `user` (`{name, role}`) and `actions`.
- Keep the logo at 32px tall; its clearspace (height ÷ 4 = 8px) is covered by the bar's padding.

## SideNav

Group: Shell

Use SideNav for a tool's main navigation.

- Provide: `items` or `sections` (`[{title, items: [{id, label, href?, icon?}]}]`), `activeId`, `onNavigate`.
- Member apps: four or five items at most, each with an `icon` and a plain label ("My credits", "Send credits", "History").
- The current item gets `aria-current="page"` and a highlighted row. Under 720px wide it becomes a horizontal row.

## AppShell

Group: Shell

Use AppShell as the page frame of an INNO-TREC web tool: TopBar, SideNav and a main area on `surface-muted`.

- Provide: `logoSrc`, `title`, `user`, `navItems` or `navSections`, `activeId`, `onNavigate`, `heading` (the page's h1) and `children` (the page content, usually Cards and StatTiles).
- Give the shell a full-height parent (`height: 100%` on html and body) so the side navigation runs to the bottom.
